channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: US May Ease Sanctions on 'Shadow Fleet' Ships Amid Rising Oil Prices
item.description: The United States is reportedly considering easing sanctions on 'shadow fleet' vessels, which transport oil from Iran, Russia, and Venezuela. This potential move follows President Trump's decision to lift some sanctions on Russian diesel. The aim is to reduce unprecedented maritime transport costs and increase the flow of refined oil products and crude oil from the Persian Gulf region, according to US officials.

item.title: Iran Builds Defenses Around Nuclear Sites Amid Potential US Conflict, WSJ Reports
item.description: Iran is constructing defensive structures around its nuclear facilities due to the possibility of conflict with the United States, according to Wall Street Journal satellite imagery analysis. The report also notes an increase in US military forces in the Middle East. This development comes amid heightened regional tensions.

item.title: 51 Students Hospitalized in Almaty School Infection Outbreak
item.description: An outbreak of infection has led to 51 students being hospitalized at the RFMSh school in Almaty. Details regarding the nature of the infection and the cause of the outbreak are still emerging. Health authorities are investigating the situation to prevent further spread and ensure the well-being of the students.

item.title: Zelensky Expresses Concern Over Declining US Support for Ukraine
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated he feels Ukraine is losing US support, despite ongoing partnership. He expressed disappointment with President Trump's recent policies, calling them a mistake and not on the "right side of history." Zelensky's remarks follow Trump's call for Ukraine to cease attacks on Russian oil facilities.

item.title: Kazakhstan Establishes National Crypto Reserve of $700 Million, $200 Million Already Invested
item.description: Kazakhstan has established a national crypto reserve valued at $700 million, with approximately $200 million already invested. The National Bank chairman's first deputy, Yerulan Jamauabayev, announced that a digital platform for issuing and operating digital financial assets has been launched. This follows the recent adoption of a law comprehensively regulating digital asset circulation and a presidential decree on developing the crypto industry.

item.title: Armenian PM Proposes Resolving Border Issues with Azerbaijan Through Territorial Exchange
item.description: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan proposed resolving the issue of enclaves and exclaves with Azerbaijan through an equal territorial exchange. He stated that border delimitation and demarcation should be based on the Almaty Declaration. Pashinyan emphasized that both countries must abandon mutual territorial claims and ensure open transport routes.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon Meets Azerbaijani Counterpart Ilham Aliyev in Baku
item.description: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon met with Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev in Baku on October 14. The official talks focused on expanding multifaceted relations and strengthening bilateral cooperation within international organizations. Further details of the meeting were not disclosed. Rahmon is scheduled to attend the 7th Conference on Interaction and Confidence-Building Measures in Asia in Baku.

item.title: Kazakhstan Mandates Prominent Shelf Space for Domestic Goods in Supermarkets
item.description: Kazakhstan is implementing new regulations effective October 20, requiring supermarkets to give domestic products prime shelf placement. Authorities aim to support local businesses and boost sales of Kazakhstani products. Experts note product placement is a science, with eye-level shelves attracting more attention and potentially increasing purchases. However, quality and price remain crucial factors for consumers.

item.title: Kazakhstan National Museum Discusses Innovative Approaches to Museum Development
item.description: A republican scientific-practical seminar, 'Museum - Educational Space: Innovative Work Directions,' was held at the National Museum in Kazakhstan. Discussions focused on modernizing museum exhibits, such as recreating Ilyas Esenberlin's 'Nomads' trilogy and showcasing the history of the dombra. Speakers emphasized the need to make historical heritage accessible and engaging for contemporary generations and foster international cooperation.

item.title: Over 50 Students Hospitalized in Almaty After Food Poisoning at Elite School
item.description: Fifty-one students at the Republican Physics and Mathematics School in Almaty have been hospitalized due to suspected food poisoning. Symptoms appeared after lunch, with children experiencing intoxication, fever, vomiting, and dehydration. The school and its dormitory have been temporarily closed pending an investigation into the mass illness.

item.title: Father and Son Detained in Almaty Region for Allegedly Shooting at Residents
item.description: A father and son are suspected of firing a weapon at residents in the village of Kosozen, Almaty region, following a road dispute. The altercation escalated into a physical fight, after which the suspects allegedly retrieved a pneumatic weapon from their home, injuring three people. Villagers demanded the family be removed.

item.title: Uzbekistan Establishes New Procedures for Business Registration via Digital Platforms
item.description: Uzbekistan has introduced new regulations for business registration, allowing legal entities and self-employed individuals to register independently through specialized digital platforms. Other economic entities will be registered at their place of operation, streamlining the process for entrepreneurs in the country.

item.title: Twenty Bangladeshi Citizens Fighting for Russia in Ukraine Reportedly Killed
item.description: Twenty Bangladeshi citizens who fought for Russia in Ukraine have reportedly died. Bangladeshi authorities suspect citizens may have been deceived into joining the conflict. Investigations are ongoing into the disappearance of 30 Bangladeshis who were promised construction jobs in Russia but were sent to military units instead.

item.title: International Organizations Urge Astana to Recognize Domestic Violence as a Separate Crime
item.description: UN treaty bodies and Human Rights Watch are calling on Kazakhstan to adopt a new law recognizing domestic violence as a distinct crime. This comes after a recent case where a woman was fatally stabbed by her ex-husband, despite reporting threats. Kazakhstan's delegation reportedly pledged to pass relevant legislation by 2024.

item.title: Navai's Director Breaks Silence After Rapper's Drug Arrest
item.description: The concert director for Russian rapper Navai, Rauf Gasanov, declined to comment on the artist's detention. Navai is currently in a temporary detention facility after a drug substance was found in his car at the "Korday" border crossing. A criminal case for attempted drug smuggling has been initiated. His planned concert in Astana was canceled due to "technical reasons."

item.title: Kazakhstan Defense Minister Holds Talks with Russian and Kyrgyz Counterparts
item.description: Kazakhstan's Defense Minister held bilateral talks with his Russian and Kyrgyz counterparts in Cholpon-Ata, Kyrgyzstan, on October 14. The meetings occurred before the CIS Defense Ministers' Council session, which will focus on military cooperation and joint plans for 2027. Discussions included current cooperation and future prospects between Kazakhstan and Russia.

item.title: CSTO Conducts 'Frontier-2026' Military Exercise in Kazakhstan Amid Regional Security Concerns
item.description: Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, and Tajikistan participated in the 'Frontier-2026' military exercise from September 13-18 in the Jetyssou region. Approximately 1,500 troops and 300 pieces of equipment, including drones, trained to repel illegal armed groups. The exercise highlights the CSTO's efforts to demonstrate interoperability amidst regional security challenges.

item.title: Central Asian states agree on measures to boost Caspian-Black Sea trade corridor efficiency
item.description: Six nations, including Azerbaijan, Georgia, Kyrgyzstan, Turkey, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan, met in Tashkent to enhance the CASCA+ trade corridor. They agreed on measures to reduce transit times and costs at intermodal nodes, simplify tariffs, and improve customs clearance. The initiative aims to strengthen the route's reliability and speed for Eurasia-to-Europe trade.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Azerbaijan Leaders Discuss Implementation of High-Level Agreements
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev in Baku to discuss bilateral relations. They reviewed progress on strategic partnership agreements, noting a 30% increase in trade turnover this year. Cooperation projects in geology, energy, transport, and other sectors were highlighted, along with cultural exchanges and regional agenda discussions.

item.title: President of Uzbekistan Arrives in Baku for Working Visit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has arrived in Baku, Azerbaijan, for a working visit at the invitation of President Ilham Aliyev. He was welcomed at Heydar Aliyev International Airport by Azerbaijani officials. The Uzbek leader will attend the 7th Summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia.

item.title: German Parliamentarians Highly Appreciate Uzbekistan's Growing Economic Potential
item.description: A parliamentary delegation from Uzbekistan met with German parliamentarians in Berlin to discuss strengthening strategic partnership, inter-parliamentary ties, and trade-economic cooperation. German officials praised Uzbekistan's economic potential, increased investments, and growing tourism. Cooperation in climate change, water management, and education was also discussed.

item.title: Cross-Border Dropper Network for Online Casinos Disrupted in Zhambyl Region
item.description: Kazakhstan's Financial Monitoring Agency has dismantled a cross-border dropper network used to service online casinos. The group created "drop farms" using bank accounts of citizens from Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, and Kyrgyzstan. They processed approximately 9.8 billion tenge through P2P platforms and cryptocurrency. Authorities seized significant amounts of cash and digital currency during raids in Turkestan and Zhambyl regions.

item.title: Kazakhstan Court Rules in Favor of Lawyer Gulnar Zhuaspaeva in Police Confrontation Case
item.description: A specialized administrative court in Kazakhstan has dismissed charges against lawyer Gulnar Zhuaspaeva, ruling there was no offense in a September 23, 2026 incident at a police station. The court issued a private ruling against the police officer involved. Zhuaspaeva had refused a personal search of her bag, citing legal protections for lawyers, and recorded the encounter.

item.title: Uzbekistan News Digest: Reforestation, Tax Exemptions, Energy Subsidies, and Legal Reforms Announced
item.description: Uzbekistan announced plans to restore 4 million hectares of pastures by 2027 and exempt transport-logistics centers from certain taxes until 2040. The government will cover 50% of electricity costs for energy-efficient greenhouses. President signed a law strengthening penalties for violence against children, and foreign nationals will need electronic permits to enter Kazakhstan from 2027.

item.title: Customs Duty Optimization Boosts Export Potential for Licorice Root Processor
item.description: Customs officials visited LLC 'Kayzen kompani' in Karakalpakstan, specializing in licorice root processing. The company exported $119,000 worth of products in 2025 and $428,000 year-to-date. Discussions focused on simplifying customs procedures for raw material import without duties, enhancing domestic sales, and increasing exports. A cooperation agreement with Afghanistan was signed.

item.title: Turkmenistan Promotes Peace Culture and Women's Leadership at UN Forum
item.description: Turkmenistan participated in a high-level UN forum in New York focused on implementing the Action Programme on the Culture of Peace, emphasizing women's leadership. Turkmenistan's Permanent Representative to the UN highlighted the connection between the culture of peace and neutrality policy, referencing a UN General Assembly resolution initiated by Turkmenistan.

item.title: Turkmenistan: Construction companies face loan defaults as families await housing
item.description: Hundreds of families in Turkmenistan are unable to move into newly built apartments near Ashgabat due to state officials delaying acceptance documents. Construction companies, unable to receive payment, are struggling to repay bank loans, leading to penalties and financial difficulties. This situation is becoming more frequent in the construction market, with some firms reportedly closing and leaving the country.

item.title: Uzbekistan participates in VII CICA Summit in Baku focusing on geo-economics and transit
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev is attending the VII Conference on Interaction and Confidence-Building Measures in Asia (CICA) Summit in Baku. The agenda prioritizes geo-economics, transit, and regional security, aiming to align national interests with Eurasian transport corridors. Uzbekistan seeks to translate political initiatives into economic growth, focusing on transport connectivity, digitalization, and sustainable development.

item.title: Uzbekistan prepares for COP31 climate summit in Turkey
item.description: Uzbekistan is actively preparing for the 31st session of the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Turkey. A working meeting, chaired by the President's Advisor on Ecology, focused on organizational aspects, promoting national environmental initiatives, and expanding international partnerships. Key priorities include presenting projects on climate change adaptation and developing a unified communication strategy to highlight Uzbekistan's contribution to global climate goals.

item.title: Saudi Arabia's Security Tested by Houthi Attacks Amid Questions on US Reliance
item.description: Recent Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia highlight concerns about the effectiveness of advanced weaponry and strategic alliances in ensuring security against asymmetric threats. The situation raises questions about the limits of US security commitments and Saudi Arabia's reliance on American support in times of crisis, despite deep military and economic ties.

item.title: Kazakhstan Leads Central Asia in Attracting Foreign Investment, State Media Reports
item.description: Kazakhstan has attracted over $155 billion in foreign direct investment, with recent years seeing significant inflows into manufacturing, chemicals, transport, communications, and finance sectors. Major investing countries include Russia, China, the US, Netherlands, Switzerland, and France, according to state media.

item.title: Uzbekistan Strengthens Penalties for Sexual Violence Against Children
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev signed a law increasing penalties for all forms of violence against children. The new legislation, effective October 14, allows for life imprisonment for sexual assault against minors under 14 and removes the statute of limitations for offenses against those under 18.

item.title: Three More Students Hospitalized After Mass Food Poisoning at Almaty School
item.description: Three additional students from the Republican Physics and Mathematics School (RFMS) in Almaty have been hospitalized, bringing the total number of affected students to 51. The students, who reside in the school's dormitory, are reported to be in stable condition. An investigation into the mass food poisoning is ongoing.

item.title: FIFA Faces New Controversy Over $4 Million Unused Office in Trump Tower, New York
item.description: FIFA is reportedly spending $4 million annually on an unused office space in New York's Trump Tower, according to The New York Times. The expensive luxury space is said to be largely vacant, sparking a new controversy surrounding the international football federation's expenditures.

item.title: Zelensky feels betrayed by Trump's stance on Russia war, says he prefers neutral US mediation
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated he feels betrayed by former US President Donald Trump's position on the war with Russia. Zelensky expressed pain over Trump's perceived bias and emphasized the need for a neutral US mediator between Kyiv and Moscow. He criticized Trump's deal for Russian diesel, fearing it would embolden Moscow.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Dissolves Parliament Ahead of Elections
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has signed a decree to prematurely terminate the powers of all levels of maslikhats (local parliaments). The Central Election Commission has been tasked with organizing and conducting early elections for these bodies. The swift action suggests prior coordination between the presidency and the election commission.

item.title: IMF Raises Uzbekistan's Economic Growth Forecast for 2026, Expects Higher External Deficit
item.description: The International Monetary Fund has increased its forecast for Uzbekistan's economic growth in 2026 to 7.8% and for 2027 to 6.5%. The IMF attributes Uzbekistan's economic stability to strong domestic demand, investment activity, remittances, and favorable gold prices. However, the report also anticipates an increase in the country's external deficit.

item.title: Turkey-Azerbaijan Relations Tested by Hijab Ban and Ties with Israel
item.description: Turkey and Azerbaijan's close relationship, based on the principle of 'one nation, two states,' appears strained. Tensions have reportedly risen due to Azerbaijan's ban on wearing hijabs in schools and its strengthening ties with Israel. Former President Heydar Aliyev indirectly criticized Turkey, asserting Azerbaijan's self-sufficiency in foreign aid.

item.title: Afghan Girls Mark International Day of the Girl Amidst Taliban Rule and Child Marriage Crisis
item.description: On the International Day of the Girl, Afghan girls are protesting their denied rights and increasing push into child marriage under Taliban rule. Facing family pressure, restrictions, and despair, some see early marriage as their only escape. Girls are using art and literature to express hope, freedom, and solidarity, highlighting their exclusion from the world.

item.title: Two Killed in Clashes Between Armed Individuals and Taliban in Afghanistan's Kandahar Province
item.description: Local sources report that two armed individuals were killed in clashes with Taliban fighters in the Spin Boldak district of Kandahar province. The Taliban's police command confirmed the incident, stating that the two individuals were allegedly planning attacks against the group. One person was killed and another wounded during the clash, with the wounded individual later succumbing to injuries.
